title: Stroke of Fate
paragraphs: NBC's 1953 alternate-history anthology asks how history might have changed if a crucial event had ended differently, then dramatizes the imagined consequences of that turning point.

Thirteen-program NBC counterfactual-history anthology. Each episode dramatizes a historical turning point under a deliberately hypothetical changed outcome, followed in many broadcasts by historian/commentator framing or news. Frozen GRH set contains the complete numbered run.
GRH documents the program through NBC counterfactual-history run (October 4, 1953 to December 27, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Lester Lewis (producer on 9 recordings, conceiver on 3 recordings, and writer on 1 recording), Mort Lewis (producer on 9 recordings, conceiver on 8 recordings, and writer on 6 recordings), Fred Weihe (director on 8 recordings), Lionel Ricou (announcer on 6 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Ted Osborne (performer on 4 recordings), Alexander Scourby (performer on 3 recordings), and John Stanley (performer on 3 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include historical turning points and contingency, alternate history and counterfactual history, historian and expert commentary, war, military decisions and conquest, United States history, and political power, succession and statecraft.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Stroke of Fate counterfactual-history radio format, Stroke of Fate premise: Earl of Essex [followed by NBC News], Stroke of Fate premise: Escape of Marie Antoinette, and Stroke of Fate premise: Germany Invades the Rhineland.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (29 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (24 shared credited people), [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (24 shared credited people), [[show|dimension-x|Dimension X]] (21 shared credited people), and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (18 shared credited people).
